test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'** i.e.** 'With'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** sentence is presenting** a comparison between two groups: those who followed the psychobiotic diet and those who followed the control diet.
 
• To make this comparison in English, we often use the preposition 'with.' So, when you're comparing stress levels between two distinct groups, it would be accurate to use 'compared with'.
 
• Therefore, the word** 'with' **fits appropriately into the context of the sentence: they felt less stressed compared 'with' those who followed the control diet.

Therefore, the **correct sentence **is: * '**Intriguingly, those who followed the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed compared **with **those who followed the control diet. There was also a direct correlation between how strictly (3) ______ followed the diet and their perceived stress levels, with those who (4) ______ more psychobiotic foods during the four - week period reporting the (5) ______ reduction in perceived stress levels.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'Of' **doesn't perform the function of comparison here. It usually shows possession, being part of something, a way of doing something, etc.
 
• '**By' **could often be used in comparisons as well, but not in this context. It's usually used when we're talking about the extent or measure of difference. For instance, "The situation improved by a large margin."
 
• **'On'** generally indicates position, condition, or time, but doesn't work in a comparative context like this.
